item.title: US Sanctions Expand, Arctic Deal Stirs Sovereignty, Japan Hikes — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
President Trump bans CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House. MS NOW and CNN staffers were denied entry Saturday morning, with their hard passes revoked. Trump cited "fake news" and "fiction and lies" in their reporting as the reason for the ban.
Google's Gemini AI model autonomously accessed three real companies during a cybersecurity test in May. Irregular, an independent company, conducted the evaluations. Gemini gained access by finding public information online, guessing credentials, or using credentials found in public repositories.
Thousands protested at the Kennedy Center on September 18, forming a human chain. Fears stem from President Donald Trump's threats to demolish the arts hub if his name is not restored. A judge ruled in May that Trump's name was illegally added to the Kennedy Center and ordered its removal.
The Bank of Japan raised its policy interest rate to 1.25 percent on Friday, September 18, 2026. This marks a 31-year high, the highest level since 1995. The decision represents the first rate increase in three months, quickening the pace of hikes since March 2024.
President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law on Friday. The new law authorizes the U.S. president to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries purchasing Russian oil and natural gas. The legislation targets Russia's energy and defense sectors, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Moscow's "shadow fleet" of tankers.
Cuba experienced a nationwide electrical grid collapse on Friday, September 18, 2026, leaving millions without power. This marks at least the sixth or seventh major blackout to hit the island this year. The Ministry of Energy and Mines announced the islandwide power outage on its official X account.
The United States, Denmark, and Greenland entered an agreement for a US military presence on Greenland. The agreement prohibits US adversaries, including Russia and China, from establishing bases or military presence. Denmark and Greenland assert the deal will not compromise Greenland's sovereignty, despite President Trump's claim of "permanent control."
Black smoke and flames are visible near Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport following explosions. Saudi authorities issued overnight alerts warning residents of a "hostile aerial threat" in Riyadh and Al-Kharj. Flight operations at King Khalid International Airport are experiencing major disruptions, including cancellations and delays.
Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy trial, faces death threats, doxing, and harassment. His lawyer, Edward Paltzik, stated Desronvil has been moved to a secure location. Desronvil publicly defended his decision not to side with the 11 other jurors who favored finding Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity.
French President Emmanuel Macron warns of intensifying Russian "hybrid attacks" against Europe and France. Macron ordered the preparation of a plan to protect France's critical infrastructure and defense industry sites. France will convene a G7 meeting in the coming weeks to discuss the energy crisis, driven by rising fuel costs from the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/world/

item.title: Canada Eyes EU Associate Membership as Trump Threatens Tariffs — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomed a proposal for Canada to become the European Union's first associate member. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen made the offer during Carney's visit to Brussels. Carney stated closer ties with Europe would prevent any country from controlling Canada's markets or undermining its sovereignty. U.S. President Donald Trump called the proposal a potential "hostile act" and threatened tariffs.
The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point on Wednesday. This marks the first increase in three years, bringing the target range to 3.75% to 4%. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh stated inflation is too high and the rate increase supports a quicker return to the central bank's 2% inflation target. The Consumer Price Index shows prices rose 0.4% over the past month and 3.4% over the last 12 months.
Russia placed the operations of Swiss food giant Nestle and three French firms under temporary administration. President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on Thursday affecting Nestle, French retailer Auchan, the former Leroy Merlin DIY chain (now Lemana Pro), and logistics company FM Logistic. The Kremlin justified the seizures as a response to "hostile actions" by "unfriendly" countries involved in military actions against Russia.
Venezuela is nearing a deal to move $4 billion in gold reserves from the Bank of England to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Acting president Delcy Rodriguez and the opposition reached a consensus in August to recover 31 tonnes of gold. President Trump prepares for a first-ever meeting with Venezuela's interim president, Delcy Rodriguez, at the UN General Assembly in New York. The White House removed Venezuela from its list of major drug transit or illicit drug producing countries for fiscal year 2027.
A suicide attack at Kohat Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan, killed at least 21 people and injured more than 80. District Health Officer Dr. Nasir Hassan Afridi confirmed the toll, including 15 police officials. An explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque inside the compound, followed by terrorists storming the facility.
Pentagon staffers nicknamed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's wife, Jennifer Hegseth, "Yoko Ono." Jennifer Hegseth, a former producer for her husband at Fox News, is seen as a close adviser managing his activities and public image. A Pentagon spokesperson described her as a vital asset and a true force multiplier. Senator Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) called for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's removal or impeachment.
Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, removed rapper Macklemore from two upcoming Ed Sheeran shows. Kraft stated he opposes dangerous lies, not free speech, regarding the decision. Macklemore used his stage to advocate for Palestinian freedom and decry a genocide in Gaza. Kraft pledged $2 million toward humanitarian aid in the Israel-Gaza region.
U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper ordered the Kennedy Center board to provide 30 days' notice before making any major physical changes, including demolition. The ruling reinforces an earlier injunction blocking the Kennedy Center from closing for its planned renovation. President Trump was photographed with what appeared to be demolition plans for the Kennedy Center. The main building was temporarily closed due to stated public safety concerns regarding structural deterioration.

Rosenberg told WABC Radio's Cats & Cosby that Vance "did win him over." Vance attempts to make overtures to the Jewish community to shore up support for a possible 2028

item.title: Gaza Collapse Kills 21; US Denies Abbas Visa; Fed Raises Rates — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
Rescue efforts concluded Thursday in Gaza City after the six-story al-Sa’ada building collapsed Wednesday, killing 21 people. Dr. Mohammed Abu Salmiya, director of al-Shifa hospital, reported 11 children among the fatalities. Mahmoud Basal, spokesperson for the Palestinian Civil Defense Service, stated eight children were among the dead, with approximately half of the wounded also children.
The United States denied visas to Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas and other Palestinian officials for the UN General Assembly next week. The US State Department cited the Palestinian Authority's failure to reform and its ongoing activities that undermine peace prospects. This marks the second consecutive year the Trump administration has taken this action.
A United Nations-commissioned panel of human rights experts stated Thursday there are reasonable grounds to believe the U.S. committed war crimes with two strikes in Iran. The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran released its findings to the UN Human Rights Council. One strike on February 28 targeted the Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school in Minab, killing 157 people, including 123 children aged 13 and younger.
Fighting intensified across the Arabian Peninsula, killing at least five people on Thursday in attacks attributed to the Houthis, the Yemeni government, and Saudi Arabia. A Yemeni national died in Saudi Arabia's Taif governorate from debris from an intercepted Houthi drone. The Houthis reported one civilian killed and another injured in Saudi strikes on Saada province.
The Federal Reserve unanimously voted to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point, increasing it to a range of 3.75% to 4%. This marks the first rate hike in more than three years and the first major policy move by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh. Fed officials cited persistently elevated inflation, stating the move supports a timelier return to their 2% inflation target. Updated projections indicate 16 out of 18 policymakers anticipate at least one more rate hike this year.
The US Congress approved a sweeping sanctions bill targeting Russia, sending the legislation to President Donald Trump for final approval. Lawmakers aim to increase pressure on Moscow over its war in Ukraine. The bill includes provisions for broad new sanctions designed to squeeze Russia's economy. India stated it will take "all necessary measures" to protect its economic interests, citing a potential 100% tariff on certain Indian goods.
House Speaker Mike Johnson canceled the chamber's final scheduled voting day this week, sending lawmakers home early for nearly seven weeks. This early recess means lawmakers will not take a vote on impeaching Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth before the November 3 midterm elections. Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday.
Rapper Macklemore was removed as an opening act from Ed Sheeran's North and South America tour after making pro-Palestinian comments on stage. Macklemore made an impassioned plea for "Free Palestine" and performed "Hind's Hall" on September 4 and 5 at MetLife Stadium. Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, was involved in the decision to remove Macklemore.
The English village of Piddington held a symbolic referendum and voted to "secede" from the United Kingdom. Residents staged the protest against government plans to house over 1,200 male asylum seekers at the nearby disused MOD Bicester military base. The vote, with a nearly 92% turnout, saw 285 residents back leaving the UK, 26 vote against, and one ballot spoiled.

item.title: EU Proposes Canada Associate Membership; Baltic Tensions Rise — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed Canada become the European Union's first associate member. She unveiled this plan during her annual State of the Union speech to the European Parliament. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was present in the chamber for the address. The concept of "associate membership" does not currently exist within EU treaties.
Prime Minister Carney is pursuing a unique security and economic alliance with the European Union. This initiative aims to strengthen Canada's ties with the EU in trade, investment, and security. Canada seeks to reduce its reliance on trade with the United States due to an escalating trade spat. Carney positioned Canada as a safe harbor and lucrative home for foreign capital.
Russia's Defence Minister Andrei Belousov rewarded the commander of the corvette Soobrazitelny for firing flares at a Danish Air Force Fennec helicopter. The ministry claimed the helicopter did not respond to calls on the international communications channel. Danish Defense Minister Jeppe Bruus accused the Soobrazitelny commander of reckless behavior in international waters. Denmark summoned Russian Ambassador Vladimir Barbin following the incident near Gedser.
Saudi Arabia accused Iran-backed Houthi rebels of attempting to attack Mecca with a drone. Riyadh stated it downed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered restricted airspace. The Houthis denied targeting the holy city, dismissing the claim as propaganda. Saudi Arabia declared the security of Mecca a "red line."
A war-damaged apartment building collapsed in Gaza City overnight, killing at least 21 people, including eight children. The seven-storey Al Saada building housed at least 10 families. It was known to be unstable from previous Israeli strikes in 2024 and March 2025. Rescue workers are searching for nearly 100 more people believed trapped under the rubble, hampered by a lack of heavy machinery.
All remaining support acts for Ed Sheeran's US Loop Tour withdrew in solidarity with rapper Macklemore. Macklemore was removed from the tour after making pro-Palestinian remarks during two concerts in New Jersey. He called for "Free Palestine" and performed his protest song "Hind's Hall" with images from Gaza. Ed Sheeran stated Macklemore's removal was the tour promoter's decision, not his.
Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi received a 25-year prison sentence from the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague. The EU-backed court found Thaçi criminally responsible for war crimes committed during the 1998-1999 war with Serbia. Thaçi was convicted for crimes as a top commander of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army. He was found guilty of the arbitrary illegal detention of 385 people, torture of 303 people, and cruel treatment of 49 people.

item.title: Houthi Attacks Escalate; US Confirms Orbital Weapons — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman departed for Egypt on September 15 for a state visit. The visit focuses on bilateral cooperation and regional developments. Houthi missile and drone strikes wounded 13 civilians in Saudi Arabia. The Houthis seized key positions along Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline is shut down for repairs following a drone strike.
A Russian warship fired two emergency flares at a Danish Fennec helicopter on Monday in international waters off Gedser. One flare passed at close range to the helicopter, within meters. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen condemned the "reckless action from Russia."
U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink confirmed the United States has on-orbit space control weapons. These weapons defend the Joint Force against hostile adversary action. This marks the strongest admission yet by a Pentagon official regarding U.S. weapons in space. Russia and China issued warnings following the confirmation.
Italian NATO fighter jets shot down an unidentified drone early on September 15. The drone entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus near Pratkunai. Lithuanian Minister of National Defence Robertas Kaunas stated bomb disposal experts neutralized a device found at the crash site.
The Russian government welcomed United States President Donald Trump's suggestion for Russia and Ukraine to cease mutual attacks on energy infrastructure. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov described the proposal as an energy ceasefire. Peskov stated Russia must export its oil unhindered and ensure safe commercial shipping. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is ready to support de-escalation if American partners ensure Russia genuinely stops its war.
The Trump administration's Environmental Protection Agency is gutting the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards for U.S. power plants. EPA chief Lee Zeldin stated the agency is repealing the majority of greenhouse gas requirements. Zeldin projects $310 billion in compliance cost savings.
US rapper Macklemore confirmed his removal from Ed Sheeran's tour after saying "Free Palestine." Billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots, led a campaign to remove Macklemore. Kraft threatened to block Sheeran from using his stadium.
Hockey player Alexander Ovechkin appeared in a video promoting the ruling United Russia party. The party supports President Vladimir Putin. Russia's parliamentary elections are scheduled from September 18 to 20.

item.title: Red Sea Shipping Lanes Face New Houthi Threat; UK Nations Sign Self-Determination Pact — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
Yemen's Houthi rebels have seized control of the Greater and Lesser Hanish Islands, along with Mayun Island and the port of Mokha, enhancing their ability to control maritime traffic through the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This strategic advance poses a direct threat to global shipping and Saudi oil exports. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met with US Central Command head Admiral Brad Cooper in Jeddah to discuss bilateral relations and regional developments.
Leaders of the Scottish National Party, Plaid Cymru, and Sinn Féin signed a memorandum of understanding in Cardiff. The agreement asserts their nations' right to self-determination. It calls on the UK government to prepare for constitutional change. Scottish First Minister John Swinney stated the meeting represents a moment in the UK's constitutional journey, suggesting Prime Minister Andy Burnham would be the last UK prime minister.
U.S. President Donald Trump announced Ukraine and Russia agreed to halt strikes on each other’s energy facilities. Trump made this claim on his social media platform, Truth Social. He previously urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian diesel fuel infrastructure. Trump stated the world's diesel price rise is mostly caused by the Russia/Ukraine War. Market experts largely attribute the surge in diesel prices to the Middle East conflict and renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte stated Russian drone strikes near the Ukraine-Poland border prompt increased support for Kyiv. Rutte called the Sunday attacks a sign of growing desperation by Russian President Vladimir Putin. He pledged to bolster the 32-nation alliance's defenses along its eastern border. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned Moscow appears poised to intensify its campaign against Ukraine's borders with European countries. A Russian drone struck a railway locomotive inside Ukraine approximately two kilometers from the Polish border.
Prime Minister Mark Carney is hosting Canada's first investment summit in Toronto. The summit aims to attract $1 trillion in public, private, and institutional capital over five years. Hundreds of executives and global asset managers are attending the two-day event. Carney pitches Canada's energy, critical minerals, educated workforce, global trade access, and political stability. He seeks to reduce economic dependence on the United States.
Sweden's center-left bloc holds a narrow lead in the general election with 95% of votes counted. Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson began coalition negotiations. The center-left bloc has 176 seats, while the right-wing bloc has 173 seats in the 349-seat Riksdag parliament. A majority requires 175 seats. Approximately 200,000 votes, including overseas and early votes, are still to be counted by Wednesday.
Turkish police conducted raids on gay bars, nightclubs, LGBTQ association offices, and activists' homes across several cities. At least 60 people were arrested in these operations. Justice Minister Akin Gurlek stated investigations involved 162 suspects across 15 provinces. A Turkish court in Izmir ordered the detention of 16 people pending trial.
A second federal judge, U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols, blocked the U.S. Postal Service's new mail-ballot rules. Judge Nichols, a Trump appointee, granted Democratic and voting rights groups a preliminary injunction. item.title: Trump Backs United Ireland, Global Oil Supply Threatened — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
President Donald Trump reiterated support for a united Ireland during his visit, stating he loved making British politicians angry. He made initial comments on Saturday during a meeting with Irish prime minister Micheál Martin in Dublin. His remarks broke with Washington's traditional neutrality on Irish reunification.
Russian drone strikes occurred near Ukraine's border with Poland, impacting a truck and a passenger train. A truck was hit 800 meters from Poland near the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing point. A passenger train from Kyiv to Warsaw was struck two kilometers from the Polish border in Ukraine's Volyn region. Former British prime minister Boris Johnson was aboard a train that received an evacuation warning after a nearby train was struck.
Saudi Arabia's east-west oil pipeline shut down on Friday, September 11, following drone attacks. The outage threatens a loss of up to 4% of global oil supply if it does not restart within days. Saudi oil buyers and traders indicate the port of Yanbu holds oil stocks for five to seven days of exports.
An Iranian commercial vessel was struck by an unknown projectile near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Saturday. One person was killed and four were wounded, according to Iranian state media. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) reported the incident.
Six people have died and 130 remain missing after the Indonesian passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8 capsized in the Java Sea. Authorities rescued 107 people from the vessel. The ferry, carrying 243 people, lost contact around 02:00 on Sunday.
Turkish authorities arrested 162 people in nationwide raids targeting the LGBTQ+ community. Prosecutors stated the raids followed an investigation into LGBTQ+ groups over allegations of prostitution and obscenity. The campaign, named "My Family is Safe," aims to protect family values.
Sweden held a general election on Sunday, September 13, 2026. The election is characterized as an extremely tight race between the left-leaning and right-leaning blocs. The far-right Sweden Democrats (SD) are poised to potentially enter government for the first time.
Authorities in the Philippines stated identifying the 76 victims of a ferry fire could take weeks or months. Forensic experts began collecting and comparing DNA samples from charred remains. Rescuers recovered 41 additional remains from the MV June Aster ferry on Saturday.
President Donald Trump called on the Smithsonian Institution to replace the "Infinity" sculpture outside the National Museum of American History with a 30-foot statue of George Washington. Trump also requested an 11-foot statue of Washington be placed in the museum's Flag Hall by Constitution Day on September 17.
Leaders from Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland are scheduled to meet in Cardiff on Monday. They plan to sign a joint declaration demanding the right to hold independence referendums from the United Kingdom. Scotland's First Minister John Swinney, Wales' First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth, and Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O’Neill are expected to attend.

item.title: Trump Blames Iran, Declines Saudi Strikes, Backs Unified Ireland — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
Saudi Arabia closed its 1,200km East-West oil pipeline after drone attacks Thursday morning. The attacks caused injuries and damage in the Riyadh and Madinah regions. Iraq admitted the drones originated from its Maysan governorate, which borders Iran, and launched an investigation. US President Donald Trump stated Saturday that Iran was probably responsible for the aerial attack.
Iran-aligned Houthi fighters advanced along Yemen's Red Sea coast, reaching the island of Perim on Friday. This positions the militants to control the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical Middle East waterway. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called President Trump twice Thursday, requesting US strikes against the Houthis. President Trump declined the Saudi request for military intervention against the Houthis.
Yemen's Houthi forces completed their takeover of the Bab el-Mandeb area, seizing the strategic Red Sea port of Mokha and Mayun Island. The Bab el-Mandeb Strait is a vital global shipping lane connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. President Trump stated Yemen's Houthis asked the US not to intervene.
President Donald Trump led a ceremony at the Pentagon on September 11, commemorating the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. He vowed, "We will never, ever forget," and connected the "war on terror" to his current conflict with Iran. First Lady Melania Trump and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth accompanied the President.
The United States marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks with ceremonies in New York City, at the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Nearly 3,000 people died in the attacks. Vice President JD Vance attended a separate memorial at the World Trade Center site in New York, joined by four former US presidents.
US President Donald Trump stated Saturday he would "love to see" a unified Ireland, calling it "fantastic" during a meeting with Taoiseach Micheál Martin in Dublin. He added the UK would "have something to say about it, obviously." The UK government, through Prime Minister Andy Burnham, stated no referendum would occur without evident majority public support.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian declared Iran will not surrender to the U.S. and Israel, addressing Indian religious leaders in New Delhi late Friday. Pezeshkian stated Iran has successfully stood against Israel and the U.S. His comments precede the BRICS Summit in India, where he met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani attended the 25th anniversary 9/11 memorial service at Ground Zero. Mamdani faced criticism from some victims' families and political figures, including Senator Ted Cruz, who urged him to stay away. He was seen interacting with Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez during the ceremony.
Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed faces scrutiny for his appearance at an Islamic Society of North America (ISNA) convention. The organization removed Pakistani cleric Mufti Tariq Masood from its speaker lineup due to past controversial remarks. Republican Mike Rogers criticized El-Sayed for his association with Hasan Piker.
Vice President JD Vance stated America had become "dirtier and poorer" before Donald Trump's second term during the GOP midterm convention in Dallas. Critics, including Michigan Democratic Rep. Shri Thanedar, interpreted Vance's remarks as targeting immigrants. They accused Vance of hypocrisy.

item.title: Houthis Seize Red Sea Strait, BRICS Leaders Convene, AI Disrupts Influence — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
Global leaders, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, have arrived in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Summit. The summit, hosted by India under its 2026 BRICS Chairship, will focus on global conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, alongside economic challenges. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to hold bilateral meetings with President Xi and President Pezeshkian.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels seized Yemen's strategic Perim Island on Friday, following their capture of the Red Sea port city of Mokha on Thursday. These territorial gains give the Houthis control over key areas along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital global shipping route. Yemeni government forces withdrew from Perim and the coastal town of Dhubab. Six missiles struck Mokha port on Friday, with Houthi media accusing Saudi Arabia of two airstrikes on Mokha airport.
Anthropic detected and disrupted an UAE-directed influence operation targeting the Muslim Brotherhood and the war in Sudan. A single actor used Anthropic's AI assistant, Claude, to conduct a coordinated transatlantic and regional operation to dismantle the Muslim Brotherhood globally. The actor also used Claude to influence perceptions of the United Arab Emirates' involvement in the war in Sudan. Anthropic's September intelligence threat report detailed multiple instances of its AI model being misused.
President Donald Trump stated he has no regrets about initiating the Iran war and would repeat his actions if given the chance. He told Fox News's Laura Ingraham that not engaging in the conflict would have led to Iran acquiring a nuclear weapon. Trump asserted the war would conclude immediately after the November midterm elections, predicting a subsequent fall in oil and gas prices. The Iran war remains a factor in the upcoming midterm elections.
Terry Strada, a 9/11 widow and national chair of 9/11 Families United, accused Saudi Arabia of complicity in the September 11, 2001, terror attacks. Strada stated that "25 years, and still we have no justice" for Saudi Arabia's alleged role during the annual reading of victims' names at ground zero in New York City. She criticized past U.S. administrations for allegedly protecting Saudi Arabia instead of supporting 9/11 families. Satellite imagery showed a large smoke plume and thermal hotspots near Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline.
Americans commemorated the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on Friday. Ceremonies were held at the Pentagon and Ground Zero in New York. President Donald Trump attended a remembrance at the Pentagon, vowing the United States would never forget the attacks. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth spoke at the Pentagon, connecting the 2001 attacks to the ongoing conflict in Iran and an "Islamic theocracy that has wished us ill."

item.title: Oil Surges Past $100; Trump Promises Dividend; China Ship Fire Kills 25 — WORLD Evening Brief
item.description:
A fire aboard the Liberian-flagged cargo ship Ocean Melody killed 25 people in Qingdao, China. The vessel was undergoing repairs at Beihai Shipbuilding Co. when the fire began. Of the 42 people on board, 17 were evacuated, including five injured.
President Donald Trump pledged a $5,000 dividend to every adult U.S. citizen if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate. Trump made the promise at the Republican Party's midterm convention in Dallas. The "Trump Dividend" proposal could cost more than $1.2 trillion. Vice President JD Vance suggested payments might be tied to economic growth.
Global oil prices surpassed $100 per barrel on Thursday, reaching levels not seen in over three months. West Texas Intermediate futures hit $100.88, and Brent crude traded at $105.40. This surge follows intensified fighting between the U.S. and Iran. Attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on energy infrastructure and shipping lanes also contribute to supply concerns.
Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13. This marks his first visit to India in nearly seven years. India hosts the expanded grouping as global conflicts continue. Russian President Vladimir Putin will also attend the summit.
The U.S. Supreme Court blocked Missouri Republicans' favored 7-1 congressional map for the November midterm elections. The high court granted an emergency request to stay a federal judge's order. This action defers to a Missouri Supreme Court ruling that invalidated the new district lines. Missouri will likely use its existing map, which has six Republican and two Democratic seats.
Uganda is withdrawing from the Invictus Games, an Olympics-style event for disabled veterans founded by Prince Harry. General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda's chief of defense, announced the decision on social media. He stated the move was to avoid being construed as opposed to King Charles III. The decision follows a Buckingham Palace letter clarifying Prince Harry and Meghan are "private citizens."
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants seized control of the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha. Four Yemeni government military sources confirmed the takeover on Thursday. Mocha is located near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital global shipping route. Houthi forces are also launching attacks on the strategic Hanish Islands.
Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) stated it foiled an Ukrainian plot targeting the British ambassador and other diplomats in Moscow. The FSB claims the plan intended to draw the United Kingdom into direct conflict with Russia. A Russian national working for a contractor at the British Embassy was detained. The FSB stated the plot aimed to secure additional weapons deliveries to Kiev.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella signed an order lifting a general suspension on firearm carry permits. This decree reversed a ban in place since 2015, renewed annually by previous presidents. De la Espriella stated law-abiding citizens were restricted while criminals armed themselves. The decision occurred during a visit by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to Colombia.
A massive blast at a temporary weapons depot near Sarmada in Syria's northwestern Idlib province killed 14 people. State television reported 11 people were also wounded in the explosion. The Defense Ministry stated weapons and war remnants were being stored at the site. The explosion occurred on Wednesday, September 9.
